topic: OneCoin: the $4 billion cryptocurrency with no blockchain

angles.angle: OneCoin took in more than $4 billion yet, prosecutors say, had no true blockchain: its bosses handed out coins that did not exist even in its own private ledger.
angles.visual: A chain of blocks snaps apart and collapses into a plain table a caret retypes.

angles.angle: At least 3.5 million people worldwide bought in between 2014 and 2016.
angles.visual: A crowd of dots spreading across a map.

angles.angle: Dr Ruja Ignatova filled Wembley Arena in 2016 and sold OneCoin on stage as the bitcoin killer.
angles.visual: An arena seen from the back rows; spotlights find a mic, the crowd lights up.

angles.angle: In October 2017 Ruja boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens and was never seen again; she is on the FBI Ten Most Wanted list.
angles.visual: A flight path draws, the radar ping fades before landing.

angles.angle: Buyers paid for trading packages and earned commissions for recruiting the next buyers: the recruits, not the coins, were the product.
angles.visual: A four-tier recruitment tree with money climbing every edge to the top.

angles.angle: Co-founder Sebastian Greenwood got 20 years in prison while the founder never faced a courtroom.
The coin's price was set by management and only ever went up [VERIFY].
angles.visual: A price line drawn by a hand, never by a market.

angles.angle: Victims can now claim from about $40 million in forfeited assets, a sliver of what was lost.
angles.visual: A huge stack beside a thin coin.
